title: Guwahati to Tawang Road Trip: Route, Stops and Sela Tunnel
seoTitle: Guwahati to Tawang Road Trip: Route, Stops, Sela Tunnel
metaDescription: Guwahati to Tawang by road: via Tezpur, Bhalukpong, Bomdila, Dirang and the Sela tunnel, with overnight stops, ILP, altitude, snow season and a week-long plan.
description: A route guide to the Guwahati to Tawang road trip: via Tezpur and Bhalukpong into Arunachal Pradesh, then Tenga, Bomdila, Dirang, the Sela tunnel and Sela Pass, and Jang to Tawang, with approximate distances, overnight stops at Dirang or Bomdila, the Inner Line Permit, altitude, winter snow, Bum La permits and a six- to eight-day return plan.
dek: The road to Tawang climbs from the Brahmaputra plains to the high passes of western Arunachal Pradesh, via monasteries, orchards and a new tunnel under Sela.

hero.alt: Snow on the slopes at Sela Pass, Arunachal Pradesh

intro: The drive from Guwahati to Tawang covers roughly 450 to 500 km. It crosses the Brahmaputra plains to Tezpur, enters Arunachal Pradesh at Bhalukpong, and climbs through forested hills to Tenga, Bomdila and the Dirang valley. The final day crosses the high country around Sela, now mostly through the Sela tunnel, which opened in March 2024, and descends past Jang to Tawang and its great monastery.
Almost everyone breaks the journey at Dirang or Bomdila, which also helps with acclimatisation before the high passes.
quickAnswer: Guwahati to Tawang is about 450 to 500 km via Tezpur, Bhalukpong, Bomdila, Dirang and the Sela tunnel, and is usually driven over two days with a night at Dirang or Bomdila. Indian visitors need an Arunachal Pradesh Inner Line Permit. October to April is best; Sela Pass has snow from about December to February. Bum La, near the border, needs a separate permit from Tawang.
takeaways: Plan two days each way, with a night at Dirang or Bomdila.
The Sela tunnel (opened March 2024) makes the route more reliable in winter.
Get your Arunachal Inner Line Permit online before travelling; it is checked at Bhalukpong.
Snow is likely around Sela from December to February, but not guaranteed.
Bum La and some areas near the border need extra permits from the district administration.

sections.heading: Permits
list: Indian visitors need an Arunachal Pradesh Inner Line Permit, available online; carry printed copies.
Bum La and some border areas need an additional permit arranged in Tawang, usually a day ahead.
Foreign nationals need a Protected Area Permit.
Rules change; check the official Arunachal portal before travel.

sections.heading: Car, driver and fuel
paras: Most travellers hire a car with a driver from Guwahati or Tezpur, as drivers know the road, the checkposts and the weather. Fuel is available in Tezpur, Bhalukpong, Bomdila, Dirang and Tawang, but fill up whenever you can. Mobile networks work in towns but drop out on long stretches, especially around Sela.

sections.heading: When to go
paras: October to April is best, with clear skies from October to December. Snow is likely around Sela and Tawang from December to February, which is beautiful but cold; the tunnel has improved winter access, but ice and snow can still slow the road. The monsoon (June to September) brings landslides on the lower sections between Bhalukpong and Bomdila.

safety: Above about 3,000 m, ascend gradually, rest on arrival and see a doctor before travel if you have heart, lung or blood-pressure conditions.
Carry snow chains or check conditions in winter.
Do not stop in restricted military areas or photograph installations.
Mountain roads close or slow down after heavy rain, snow or landslides; check road status and weather updates each morning and avoid driving after dark.
Permits, tolls, entry fees, pass openings and road works change; check official sources shortly before you travel.
Distances and driving times are approximate and vary with traffic, weather, road works and stops.
packing: Warm layers, gloves and a warm hat
Cash; ATMs are limited beyond Bomdila

faqs.q: How far is Tawang from Guwahati by road?
faqs.a: About 450 to 500 km via Tezpur, Bomdila, Dirang and the Sela tunnel.

faqs.q: How many days does the drive take?
faqs.a: Two days each way, with a night at Dirang or Bomdila.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit for Tawang?
faqs.a: Yes. Indian visitors need an Arunachal Pradesh Inner Line Permit; Bum La needs an additional permit.

faqs.q: When can I see snow on the way to Tawang?
faqs.a: Usually from December to February around Sela, though it is never guaranteed.

faqs.q: Is the Guwahati to Tawang road good?
faqs.a: It is mostly paved but winding and slow, with landslides in the monsoon.
